newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkish state banks' lost 32.16 trln lira in H1.
newsitem.headline: Turkish state banks' lost 32.16 trln lira in H1.

text.p: Turkish state banks posted a total of 32.16 trillion lira of losses in the first half of 1996 in sharp comparison to a total 8.15 trillion lira profit in the same period last year, a Treasury report said.
The report on "Turkish banks' financial structure and development" said private banks raised their profits in the first six months of 1996 by 91.5 percent from a year ago to 67.48 trillion lira.
Investment and development banks' profits surged 615.4 percent to 12.9 trillion lira in the first six months when compared to a year ago.
Because of the state banks' losses, total bank profits rose slightly to 53.58 trillion lira in first half 1996 from 50.38 trillion in the same period last year.
"State banks' losses caused overall first half bank profits to drop by 39 percent in real terms," the report said.

"A fall in banks' foreign borrowing in real terms, macroeconomic uncertainties and rising costs (interest rates) due to increased need for public borrowing, decreasing short currency positions and insufficient equities badly affected banks' income sheets," it added.
A total of 62 Turkish banks, including 12 investment and five state banks, had made a 104.71 trillion lira profit at the end of 1995.
